en: The sixteen honored ones of the Bhadrakalpa are outside that wheel-maṇḍala;
among the thousand Buddhas of the Bhadrakalpa, these sixteen are the preeminent leaders. Maitreya holds a *kamaṇḍalu*.
Amoghapāśa with lotus eyes, Brahmā holding a palm-leaf manuscript to dispel sorrow,
Acala with a trident to eliminate evil, Gandhahasti holding a lotus,
Mahāvīra brandishing a spear, and Gaganagañja with jewel-light.
The Banner of Wisdom with its insignia, the Lotus of Immeasurable Light,
Bhadrapāla holding a precious vase, Jālinīprabha with his parasol,
Candraprabha with his crescent-moon banner, and Anantamati with his palm-leaf manuscript.
Discerning the clouds of accumulated offerings, the single-pronged Vajragarbha,
and the five-wisdom mudrā of Samantabhadra; the seed-syllable is the initial letter A,
while the syllable HŪṂ presses down upon the ground to the left.
The respective mantras are as follows:
In the outer precinct of the Vajradhātu, the earth-dwelling and space-faring deities are briefly said to be of five classes; those who are wrathful are designated by the syllable HŪṂ.
Arranged across twenty days, with lotus leaves serving as seats:
in the northeast is Nārāyaṇa, in the form of a Rākṣasa holding a discus;
Kumāra, in the form of a youth with a bell-seal; and the god who crushes the yakṣas.
At the eastern gate of the precious parasol, Brahmā holds a red lotus like a celestial being;
Śakra, in the form of a youth, holds a single-pronged vajra; the Fire God (Agni) is in the southeast, red in color, with a triangle as his emblem;
and the Sun God (Sūrya) is in the form of a youth.
Vajrabhakṣa holds a garland; Yama-daṇḍa is red in color with the mudrā of the staff.
Aṅgāraka is a mass of fiery light, red in color, with a terrifying appearance;
he is the lord of the rākṣasas in the southwest, holding a mallet along with his retinue. Bṛhaspati is celestial and holds a club.
Vajrāmbhasa Yakṣa is at the western gate, holding a bow and arrow;
Varuṇa holds a noose. Next, place the form of the youth Candradeva.
In the northwest corner is Vāyu, with a banner; he has the form of a Rākṣasa and is ash-colored. Vajramukha holds a hook and is black.
The Subduing Vajra Sword: To the east of the gate is Mahābala, golden in color;
he holds a stūpa in his palm and a jeweled staff, while in his left hand he holds an *īśāna* trident and a *kambala* garment.
The respective mantras are as follows:
"Such is the host of Great Devas, whose majestic power manifests in many ways;
together with their queens and retinues, they all abide within the maṇḍala."
One should fully explain and reveal this; one should worship the deity Nakata, who resides to the east of the northern gate.
His mantra is as follows:

"Oṃ vajranivārya-kaca svāhā. This concludes the sixteen deities. On the sixteenth day of the fifth month of the Renxu year, based on the manuscript from Chijik-in in Jingzhao and collated with the manuscript from Shiba-bō at Fuyōzan, this was carved into printing blocks and circulated in the world.
Recorded by the Shamon Kaidō, residing at Myōon-in in Hase, Ōmō.
